problem: Can the historical c/k immediately preceding -(a)meke in Steffel's color words be identified with the modern color modifier -ka?
direct_answer: Not yet demonstrated, but the retention-plus-specialization hypothesis is now substantially better motivated than before.

hypotheses.label: Retention of an older stative *-ga + participial *-ame chain
hypotheses.mechanism: Historical color -cameke/-gameke reflects an older stative/derivational ga + ame sequence plus final -ke, with orthographic or phonological variation in the consonant.
support: Modern dialectal -game is explicitly analyzed as -ga + -ame.
Guadalaxara 1683 already attests a stative gamek chain.
Steffel's color forms have -kameke~-kame surface variants that align closely with modern -ka-me.
problems: No published historical analysis yet identifies the color c/k itself as stative -ga.
The unpublished 1799 grammar cannot presently be audited in full.
Merrill explicitly leaves segmentation of schiógameke uncertain.

hypotheses.label: Later reanalysis of inherited -kame(ke) as modern -ka + -me
hypotheses.mechanism: An older opaque or differently segmented chain became resegmented in modern color morphology as degree/color modifier -ka followed by participial -me.
support: Merrill's historical suffix inventory does not independently list a color -ka.
Modern grammars provide a transparent root + -ka + -me analysis that need not have been synchronically available to eighteenth-century speakers.
problems: The existence of older ga+ame and 1683 gamek makes a completely new late segmentation less economical than previously thought.
Historical truncated color forms already produce kame strings virtually identical to modern -ka-me.

hypotheses.label: Retention followed by analogical/semantic specialization in the color system
hypotheses.mechanism: An inherited stative/participial ga+ame(+ke) domain survived formally, while the color subsystem later regularized or specialized the pre-participial element as -ka 'color subido' and contrasted it with -na 'color bajo/becoming'.
support: Combines the deep history of *-ame and ga+ame with the explicit modern color contrast -ka versus -na.

Historical color -na has its own direct bridge to modern color -na, suggesting that the color paradigm could have reorganized older general verbal/stative morphology into a specialized semantic opposition.
Historical -kameke~-kame and modern -ka-me are directly linked at the surface level in black and white.
problems: The timing and mechanism of semantic specialization are not independently dated.
Color-specific historical -ga/-ka remains unsegmented in the published Steffel evidence.

epistemic_status.reason: H3 explains both the older ga+ame/gamek evidence and the specialized modern -ka/-na color opposition without forcing modern segmentation unchanged onto the eighteenth century.

next_tests: Locate or obtain a transcription of Steffel's 1799 grammar and search adjective/stative morphology for ca/ka/ga.
Audit Burgess 1984 and Burgess-Kempton-MacLaury 1983 directly for the internal analysis and semantics of Western Tarahumara color -ka.
Find historical color predicates beyond red that contain independently segmentable -na or ga/ka.
Test whether k~g alternation is regular in the relevant morphological environment rather than merely orthographic.
